key.title: Make a key
key.intro: hubspot reads your deals, contacts and companies from one HubSpot account. It changes nothing there.
key.service: A super admin does this once, in HubSpot: open **Development → Keys → Service keys**, create a key, name it *WireCat*, and give it these read scopes:
key.leads: On Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise, add `crm.objects.leads.read` to read leads too. Add `tickets` if you want `api` to read tickets.
key.private.title: Use a legacy private app instead
key.private: HubSpot calls private apps legacy, but their tokens still work. Give the private app the same read scopes, then copy its access token from the app's **Auth** tab.
token.title: Paste the key
token.where: Copy the service key, or the private app's access token. It starts with `pat-`.
token.label: Service key or access token
token.hint: Kept in your system keyring or, without one, in a file only you can read.
token.rights: The key reads only what its scopes allow. Each profile signs in to its own HubSpot account: a second profile on the same account is refused.
check.title: Checking the key
check.body: hubspot asks HubSpot which account the key belongs to. It saves the key only if HubSpot answers.
failed.title: The check did not pass
failed.body: The key did not pass hubspot's check, so nothing was saved. Check the key and your connection, then try again.
done.title: Connected
done.body: The profile is ready. Copy your deals and their contacts and companies into WireCat, then list the open ones:
